title: *Interplay of climate change-exacerbated rainfall, exposure and vulnerability led to widespread impacts in the Mediterranean region* (World Weather Attribution)
temporal_coverage: Storm Daniel, Sep 2023; counterfactual climate comparison
methodology: Observational products plus climate-model attribution analysis of extreme rainfall
limitations: Large statistical uncertainty for Libya; single-event analysis; does not attribute dam failure or total disaster losses to climate change.

title: *Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Libya 2024* (SIPRI)
geographic_coverage: National with Derna, Fezzan and other subnational examples
methodology: Synthesis of climate, migration, water, conflict and governance datasets/literature
limitations: Short synthesis rather than original causal study; some projection parameters/models are not reproduced; local examples cannot be generalized nationally. Copyright notice reserves reuse.

title: *Environment and Climate Change - Libya* (UNDP)
methodology: UNDP contextual synthesis and programme description
limitations: No explicit research methodology; programme intentions are not evidence of effectiveness; page lacks a clear publication/update date.

title: *Final Evaluation: Support to Energy Transition and Climate Change Mitigation in Libya*
methodology: Desk review, semi-structured interviews, participant survey and triangulation
limitations: 14 interviewees; several important institutions unreachable; survey 58/193 trainees; limited female representation; predates some 2026 policy developments.

title: *National Drought Management Strategy and Action Plan for Libya* (UNDP)
limitations: Publication establishes a strategy, not implementation or effectiveness; full implementation evidence was not available.

title: *Libya Launches 2050 National Water Security Strategy to Combat Scarcity and Build Climate Resilience* (UNDP)
methodology: Reports official endorsement following multi-year national dialogue
limitations: Strategy targets are prospective; no independent outcome evaluation yet.

title: *UN 2.0 in Action: Building Climate Resilience in Libya* (The United Nations in Libya)
limitations: Outputs and reported reach are not independent impact estimates; causal effectiveness cannot be inferred.

title: *Libya Operational Update - 31 October 2025* (UNHCR)
geographic_coverage: National with Alkufra and other operational locations
methodology: Registration, protection monitoring, household/field information and operational data
limitations: Refugee-focused rather than climate-focused; arrival estimates vary by method; cannot establish climate causality.

title: *Libya Country Strategic Plan (2023-2025)* (The United Nations in Libya)
methodology: Country needs assessment, UN common analysis, food-security/livelihood evidence
limitations: Older baseline; programme design is not evaluation; climate, conflict and COVID-related constraints are often intertwined.

title: *Libya - Country Overview* (World Bank)
methodology: World Bank country monitoring and analytical synthesis
limitations: Not a dedicated climate-FCV study; national indicators can hide regional variation.

title: *Joint World Bank, EU, UN Report Assesses Damages Caused by Catastrophic Flooding in Libya* (World Bank)
organization: World Bank / European Union / United Nations
temporal_coverage: Sep 2023 event and immediate recovery assessment
methodology: Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment using remote information, imagery, public and partner data
limitations: Event-specific and eastern; publication page summarizes the full RDNA; remote methods and incomplete access create uncertainty.

title: *Libya: Storm Daniel and Flooding Situation Report No. 4*
methodology: Field/partner assessments, humanitarian coordination data and UNICEF response monitoring
limitations: Early emergency snapshot; casualty and displacement figures subsequently changed; response outputs do not establish longer-term effectiveness.

title: *National Communication submissions from Non-Annex I Parties* (UNFCCC)
limitations: Covers National Communications, not the full universe of domestic climate policy; blank registry fields do not imply absence of all domestic climate activity.

title: Libya Country Brief
organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Global Information and Early Warning System
temporal_coverage: Weather and crop conditions through July 2026; 2026 harvest and 2026/27 import forecasts.
methodology: FAO GIEWS synthesis of rainfall, crop, price and food-security data.
limitations: Forecasts are not verified outcomes; no climate attribution or detailed local food-security estimates.

title: Rapid flood impact assessment on water management infrastructure and agriculture in Eastern Libya in 2023
organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
temporal_coverage: Assessment of the September 2023 floods; FAO summary published May 2025.
methodology: FAO summary of a rapid geospatial assessment using flood extent, land cover, irrigated cropland, population and farmer-vulnerability indicators.
limitations: The linked full report download returned 403; only the complete official FAO summary page was inspected, so detailed underlying methods and district tables were not reviewed.

title: Situational Assessment of The South of Libya 2024
organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator's Office in Libya
temporal_coverage: 2024 assessment version; synthesis of 2018–2023 agency and INGO assessments.
methodology: UN inter-agency assessment of governance, services, social cohesion and environmental conditions in southern Libya.
limitations: The PDF exceeded reader limits; claims use only official indexed executive-summary and climate/DRR excerpts.

title: The United Nations Libya Annual Results Report 2025
temporal_coverage: Reported United Nations results achieved during 2025; report published 3 May 2026.
methodology: United Nations country-team annual results report describing partner-supported outputs and reported beneficiaries.
limitations: The 46.9 MB report exceeded the reader limit; claims use only official indexed excerpts on printed p.34 and are implementer-reported, not an independent impact evaluation.
